strings.kb_betterment: Tax on the gain from selling a home or land. Sellers of a sole residence can be exempt under certain conditions.
strings.kb_boi: The rate the Bank of Israel sets about eight times a year to cool or boost the economy. It drives prime, mortgages and the interest you earn on deposits.
strings.kb_brackets: Israeli income tax is progressive: each slice of income is taxed at its own bracket rate. Moving into a higher bracket only raises tax on the part above it, not on your whole salary.
strings.kb_breakeven: The volume or revenue at which a business exactly covers all its costs. Above it, you start making a profit.
strings.kb_btl: Payroll deductions that fund benefits (unemployment, maternity, disability, old age and more) and the health system. The rate is low on the first part of your pay and higher above it.
strings.kb_capgain: Tax on the real gain from selling shares, funds, crypto and other assets — usually 25%. Losses can be offset against gains in the same year.
strings.kb_compound: When earnings are added to the principal and start earning too. The longer the time, the bigger the effect — so starting early matters far more than the deposit size.
strings.kb_cpi: A monthly index from the Central Bureau of Statistics that tracks prices of a basket of goods and services. "CPI-linked" loans and savings are updated by it.
strings.kb_credit: A credit or instalment deal with interest adds cost to a purchase. Check the effective rate and the total you will pay before agreeing.
strings.kb_crypto: Digital currencies like Bitcoin whose prices swing widely. In Israel, gains from selling or swapping them are subject to capital gains tax.
strings.kb_debt: Two common methods: the "snowball" pays the smallest debt first for momentum; the "avalanche" pays the highest-interest debt first, saving more interest.
strings.kb_div: Part of a company's profit paid out to shareholders. In Israel it is usually taxed at 25%, and 30% for a major shareholder.
strings.kb_effective: The true yearly cost of a loan, including fees and payment frequency. It is the right way to compare offers from different banks.
strings.kb_emergency: Cash set aside for emergencies, usually 3–6 months of expenses, so a lost income or a sudden bill does not push you into debt.
strings.kb_equal: Each month you repay the same share of principal plus interest. Payments start high and fall over time, and total interest is lower than with Spitzer.
strings.kb_fire: Saving and investing hard to reach financial independence and retire early. A common rule of thumb: build 25 times your yearly spending (the "4% rule").
strings.kb_gross: Gross is pay before deductions. Net is what reaches your account after income tax, National Insurance, health tax and the pension contribution.
strings.kb_hishtalmut: A medium-term savings fund your employer pays into, usually available after 6 years. Up to a ceiling its gains are free of capital gains tax — one of the most worthwhile savings.
strings.kb_infl: A general rise in prices over time. With 3% inflation, ₪100 buys next year roughly what ₪97 buys today — so money that is not invested loses value.
strings.kb_lease: Renting a car for a fixed term with a monthly payment. Compare the full cost, including any down payment and end-of-term payment, with buying in cash or on finance.
strings.kb_leave: Paid days off that build up with seniority and job scope. Unused days are paid out when the job ends.
strings.kb_linked: In a CPI-linked loan the balance is updated by the price index. With inflation, the debt and the payment grow even if the rate is fixed.
strings.kb_mortgage: A home loan secured by the home itself. In Israel it is usually built from several tracks, each with its own rate and linkage.
strings.kb_networth: Everything you own (savings, investments, home) minus everything you owe (mortgage, loans). The best measure of your finances and progress over time.
strings.kb_notice: How far in advance whoever ends the employment (employee or employer) must give notice. It depends on seniority and on monthly versus hourly pay.
strings.kb_pension: Mandatory retirement savings: you and your employer put a share of your salary in every month (including a severance part), and it is invested until retirement. Low management fees make a big difference to the final amount.
strings.kb_points: Points that lower your monthly income tax. Each point has a fixed value updated every year, given for residency, gender, children, a degree, army and reserve service and more. Enter yours in the personal profile in Settings.
strings.kb_prepay: A fee the bank may charge when you repay a loan early, mainly on fixed-rate tracks when market rates have fallen since you took it.
strings.kb_prime: The base rate Israeli banks charge on loans. It is always the Bank of Israel rate plus 1.5%, so when the Bank of Israel changes its rate, prime and every loan tied to it change right away.
strings.kb_purchase: Tax paid when buying a home or property. A sole home has lenient brackets; investors and additional homes pay more.
strings.kb_rate: The official exchange rate the Bank of Israel publishes every business day. Banks, exchange offices and card companies add a margin, so the rate you get differs a little.
strings.kb_refi: Replacing your current mortgage with a new one on better terms. Compare the interest saved with the early-repayment fee and costs.
strings.kb_rental: Residential rent has three options: exemption up to a monthly ceiling, a 10% track on gross income, or regular bracket tax with expenses deducted. The calculator compares them.
strings.kb_rentbuy: Comparing renting and investing your equity with buying on a mortgage. The answer depends on interest rates, the alternative return on your money and house-price growth.
strings.kb_reserve: Active reservists can get extra credit points based on the days they served the previous year. Enter the days in the personal profile in Settings and the calculation includes them.
strings.kb_savegoal: An amount you want to reach by a certain date. The calculator shows how much to put aside each month, allowing for returns and inflation.
strings.kb_selfemp: An exempt dealer charges no VAT and has a yearly turnover cap; a licensed dealer charges VAT and offsets VAT on expenses. Both pay their own income tax and National Insurance.
strings.kb_severance: Usually one month's salary per year worked, for an employee who was dismissed and in some cases one who resigned. Part of it is tax-free up to a ceiling.
strings.kb_spitzer: A repayment method with a fixed monthly payment. At first most of it is interest; later most of it reduces the principal.
strings.kb_tracks: The main tracks: prime (floats with prime), fixed unlinked, fixed CPI-linked, and variable every five years. A good mix balances a stable payment against total cost.
strings.kb_vat: A tax added to most goods and services. In Israel it is 18% (since January 2025): price with VAT = price × 1.18, price before VAT = price ÷ 1.18.
strings.kb_yield: The gain from an investment as a percentage over a period. An average yearly return lets you compare investments held for different lengths of time.

strings.n_ap: Use = power in watts × hours. Air conditioners and fridges do not run at full power all the time, so this is an upper estimate. Home tariff from July 2026: 63.52 agorot per kWh incl. VAT.
strings.n_be: Fixed costs and variable cost per unit are assumed constant. Tax is excluded.
strings.n_bnMat: 2026 estimate: maternity pay = pay in the 3 months before birth divided by 90, up to 1,752.33 ₪ a day. Full entitlement of 15 weeks (105 days) after working 10 of the last 14 months or 15 of 22, and 8 weeks after 6 of 14. If better, 6 months divided by 180 is checked too. Income tax and contributions are deducted.
strings.n_bnUn: 2026 estimate: daily pay = last 6 months of pay divided by 150, and the benefit is tiered (lower rates under 28). Cap: 550.76 ₪ a day for the first 125 days and 367.17 ₪ after. Monthly figure uses 25 days. Income tax and contributions are deducted, and there are waiting days at the start.
strings.n_capital: Rates: securities gains 25% (30% for a substantial shareholder), dividends 25%/30%, deposit interest 15% and other interest 25%. Surtax: 3% on total income above ₪721,560 plus 2% on its capital part. Foreign withholding and other offsets are not included.
strings.n_cb: 2026 benefit value: 2.48% of the list price a month, up to a price cap of 596,860 ₪. Monthly reduction: hybrid 580 ₪, plug-in 1,150 ₪, electric 1,380 ₪. The value is added to taxable income, so the cost is how much your net pay drops. The Tax Authority has a simulator for exact figures.
strings.n_cc: Interest is computed monthly on the balance. Actual terms depend on the issuer and transactions.
strings.n_cl: Cost includes the down payment, payments, yearly costs and an alternative return on the cash, less resale value. Leasing covers the term only, with no buyout at the end.
strings.n_da: Excludes fees and tax. Averaging lowers your break-even price but does not guarantee a profit.
strings.n_div: Dividends are computed on shares held at the start of each year. With reinvestment, shares are bought at the year-end price. Tax rates are examples; actual withholding depends on the account type and the country of the share.
strings.n_dp: Avalanche saves the most interest; snowball gives quick wins. A cleared debt’s payment rolls to the next. Fixed rates, no indexation or fees.
strings.n_ds: The real price per item helps compare deals. For example, 1+1 equals 50% off only if you really need both.
strings.n_ec: 2026 rates: employer National Insurance 4.51% up to 7,703 ₪ and 7.6% above, pension 6.5% and severance 8.33% (or 6% by agreement). Recreation pay, vacation and sick days are already part of pay and not added.
strings.n_ev: Petrol price for October 2026: 8.27 ₪ a liter self-service. Home electricity from July 2026: 63.52 agorot per kWh incl. VAT. Public charging costs more. Depreciation, insurance and fees are not included.
strings.n_fi: The safe withdrawal rate is a research rule of thumb, not a promise, and depends on markets, longevity and tax. Capital needed = yearly spending divided by the rate. Deposit and return are held constant.
strings.n_fl: Assumes 9 holidays a year and 2026 self-employed income tax and National Insurance: 52% of the National Insurance part (not health) is deducted from income, and the National Insurance base is worked out the way Bituach Leumi does. Credit points are as you entered them. Pension deposits are not included, so add them to expenses.
strings.n_fr: Order: debts, then emergency fund, then investing up to the target (yearly spending divided by the withdrawal rate). All surplus goes to the current stage. Return is constant; inflation, tax and changing spending are ignored. A roadmap, not a forecast.
strings.n_inFuture: An estimate using the fixed inflation rate you chose. Actual inflation varies year to year.
strings.n_inPast: Based on the official CBS December-to-December change in the consumer price index. The current year uses the latest published index. For exact month-by-month linkage, use the index linkage calculator.
strings.n_inReal: Real return = (1 + return) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1. Before tax and fees.
strings.n_jo: Net pay uses 2026 rules, with a 6% employee pension deduction and 2.5% study fund when the employer deposits. A company car adds tax but saves costs, so enter what it saves you. Full package = net + all savings deposits + car and perks.
strings.n_kh: Employees: the employer deposits up to 7.5% and the employee 2.5%, tax-free up to a salary of 15,712 ₪ a month (2026). Self-employed: deduct 4.5% of income up to 13,203 ₪ a year, with capital gains exemption on deposits up to 20,566 ₪. The money is liquid after 6 years (or 3 near retirement age).
strings.n_ks: Bituach Leumi deposits ₪58 a month for every child until 18 (2026), and parents can add another ₪58 from the child allowance. Grants: born before 2017, ₪582 at 18. Born from 2017, ₪291 at 3 and ₪291 at bar/bat mitzvah. Leaving the money until 21 adds another ₪582. Amounts are updated every year, and the return depends on the track.
strings.n_lc: Effective rate uses the net amount after the opening fee and the monthly payments. Assumes an annuity schedule with no indexation.
strings.n_lcPrime: Prime-based offers assume Prime stays at today's {p}; in practice it moves with the Bank of Israel rate.
strings.n_leave: Recuperation days in the private sector: 5 in year 1, 6 in years 2-3, 7 in years 4-10, 8 in 11-15, 9 in 16-19, 10 from year 20, at ₪451.50 a day in 2026. Sick days are not paid out. The divisor and vacation days depend on your contract. Check your contract or the relevant order.
strings.n_lk: Linkage uses the ratio of the two index values. For a binding contract, check the CBS linkage calculator too.
strings.n_lkBuild: The CBS residential construction input index, chained to the latest base. Usually used for payments to a developer on a new home.
strings.n_lkCpi: The CBS general consumer price index, chained to the latest base.
strings.n_lt: 25% on the real gain after expenses and inflation, plus surtax on high income. Residence exemption: if the price exceeds the ceiling, a proportional share is taxed. Eligibility has conditions such as time between sales. An estimate.
strings.n_mc: Bank of Israel rules: financing up to 75% for a first home, 70% when upgrading and 50% for investment, terms up to 30 years, and payments up to 50% of income. Purchase tax, lawyer, agent and other costs paid from equity are not included.
strings.n_mf: Deposit fees come off every deposit, balance fees off everything saved. Legal caps: pension funds up to 6% of deposits and 0.5% of balance; provident and study funds up to 4% and 1.05%. You can ask for a discount or move to a cheaper fund.
strings.n_mortgage: Rates in the form are editable examples, not a bank offer. Bank of Israel limits: financing of 75%, 70% or 50% by buyer type; up to two thirds in variable tracks; payment ratio up to 50%. Purchase tax, insurance and fees are not included.
strings.n_notice: Based on the advance notice law. Days are calendar days. Value is monthly pay times days over 30. A contract may grant more.
strings.n_nw: The stage is approximate: negative worth, non-mortgage debt, cash below 3 months of expenses, passive income below expenses, or fully covered. A mortgage is not treated as costly debt. An estimate, not advice.
strings.n_ot: Under the Hours of Work and Rest Law: a full week is 42 hours and hourly pay is based on 182 hours a month. The first two extra hours a day pay 125%, beyond that 150%. Work on the weekly rest day or a holiday pays at least 150%. Minimum wage from April 2026: 6,443.85 ₪ a month or 35.40 ₪ an hour. Net pay is an estimate.
strings.n_points: Child points are counted per parent under 2026 rules; if both parents work, check how points are split between you. A resident man starts at 2.25 points and a woman at 2.75.
strings.n_pp: Prepaying is a safe return equal to the loan rate. Investing carries risk and returns are not guaranteed. Prepayment fees and indexation are not included.
strings.n_prDep: A prime-linked deposit rate moves with the BoI rate. This assumes it stays the same.
strings.n_prLoan: Calculated on the nominal rate ÷ 12, as banks do. With an annuity the payment is recalculated when the rate changes. Excludes indexation, fees and insurance.
strings.n_prOd: An estimate for a constant overdraft. Banks actually charge on the daily balance, usually quarterly.
strings.n_prSimple: Simple interest is on the principal only; compound interest also earns on accrued interest.
strings.n_pt: Brackets reflect early 2026 per public sources and are updated periodically. Check the Tax Authority simulator before a deal. Special reliefs, such as for disabled buyers, are not included.
strings.n_rb: Whoever pays less each month invests the difference at your stated return. Investment tax, land tax and rate changes are not included. The result is very sensitive to the price and rent assumptions.
strings.n_refi: Compares remaining payments on the current loan with payments plus costs on the new one. Indexed or variable loans can change. Differences in term are not adjusted.
strings.n_rental: Full exemption up to ₪5,654 a month. Between ₪5,654 and ₪11,308 the exemption shrinks, and above ₪11,308 there is none. The 10% track is a final tax on gross rent with no deductions. In the regular track rent is added to your other income. Tracks are not available in every case, for example with several rented properties. Check with the Tax Authority.
strings.n_rt: Assumes a constant return and inflation, both of which vary in practice. Income is drawn until the planning age. Tax on pension or withdrawals is not included.
strings.n_sCar: Work car: the 2026 benefit value is 2.48% of the list price a month (up to a price cap of ₪596,860), minus the hybrid, plug-in or electric reduction and minus your contribution. It never reaches your bank account, but you pay income tax, National Insurance and health tax on it.
strings.n_sCarBr: The benefit sits on top of your pay, so it is taxed at your highest brackets. 2026 brackets: 10% up to ₪7,010, 14% up to ₪10,060, 20% up to ₪19,000, 31% up to ₪25,100, 35% up to ₪46,690 and 47% above.
strings.n_salary: Estimate for a resident employee: 2026 tax brackets, National Insurance and health tax, and a 35% credit on the employee pension contribution. It excludes other benefits such as children, qualifying localities or employer study fund contributions. Employer cost assumes 6.5% pension and 6% severance.
strings.n_salary2: An estimate for a resident employee: 2026 brackets, National Insurance and health (1.04% and 3.23% up to ₪7,703; 7% and 5.17% up to ₪51,910) and a 35% credit on the employee pension deposit. Employer deposits above the tax-free limits (pension above 7.5% of ₪33,290, severance above 8.33% of ₪44,100, study fund above 7.5% of ₪15,712) are added as income. A bonus is spread as a monthly average, so the result is close to, but not the same as, the payslip in the month the bonus is paid.
strings.n_selfemp: The self-employed pay National Insurance and health: 7.7% up to ₪7,703 a month and 18% up to ₪51,910. As Bituach Leumi does, the base is the income after deducting 52% of the National Insurance part (not health) and the pension deduction, and never below ₪3,442 a month. The same 52% of the National Insurance part only is also deducted from taxable income. Pension: a 35% credit on up to 5.5% of qualifying income and a deduction of up to 11%, up to a ₪232,800 ceiling. Advances, adjustments and a company comparison are not included.
strings.n_sev: Calculated as last salary times years. The exemption is the lower of last salary and the ceiling, times years. Spreading is approximated at one year per year of service up to 6. Rules differ if funds were deposited in a provident fund. An estimate, not tax advice.
strings.n_sg: Deposits at the end of each month, interest compounded monthly. Returns are not guaranteed.
strings.n_sp: Income-based splitting is proportional to each person’s income.
strings.n_sp2: Split equally, by income, percentages, parts or by what each ordered. Settle up works out who pays whom so everyone pays the same.
strings.n_tax: Income tax on earned income by 2026 brackets. The surtax is 3% on the part above ₪721,560 a year. Amounts are in shekels regardless of the display currency.
strings.n_tax2: Income tax on earned income by 2026 brackets. Surtax: 3% on all income above ₪721,560 a year, plus 2% on the capital part of it. The pension credit is 35% on up to 7% of income, up to a ceiling.
strings.n_tr: An estimate only, using the 2026 tax brackets and credit points. You can claim a refund for the last 6 years with form 135 or in the Tax Authority personal area. Common reasons: working part of the year, several employers, donations, children, a degree and reserve duty.
strings.n_up: The price is worked out per kilo, liter or unit, including multipacks, so different sizes can be compared.
strings.n_upMix: Items in different measures (weight, volume or units) are compared only within the same group.
strings.n_vat: Rates for other countries are standard rates, for illustration. Israel's rate is 18% since January 2025.
strings.n_wd: Israeli rest days counted as holidays: Rosh Hashanah (2), Yom Kippur, Sukkot, Simchat Torah, Passover (first and seventh), Shavuot and Independence Day. Holiday eves, intermediate days and election days are not counted, so check your work agreement.
strings.note: Calculations are for illustration only and are not financial or tax advice. Tax and wage data are for Israel, 2026. Exchange rates are for reference only, not transaction rates.

strings.rc_appPwOnly: This is the app password only, not your email password. Choose a unique one not used anywhere else.
strings.rc_body:
Hello,

This is the recovery key for the account {n} in the financial calculator:

{c}

To verify the email: type the key in the app, under Settings → Account → Email verification.
Forgot your password? On the sign-in screen tap "Forgot password", type the username and the key, and choose a new password. All data is kept.
strings.rc_bodyKeep: Keep this email and do not share it: anyone with the key can set a new password for the account.
strings.rc_checking: Checking that the email is free…
strings.rc_codeShort: The recovery key has 20 characters, like XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX.
strings.rc_codeWrong: The key is wrong. Copy it from the latest email you sent.
strings.rc_copied: Message copied. Paste it into a new email to yourself.
strings.rc_doneIn: The new password is set and all data was kept.
strings.rc_go: Recover and set a new password
strings.rc_intro: If you forget your password, a verified email lets you set a new one without losing data. There is no server: you send yourself an email with a recovery key, and the address is stored only in your account.
strings.rc_mailBad: The email address is not valid.
strings.rc_mailCheckFail: Could not check that the email is free. Check the connection and try again.
strings.rc_mailTaken: This email already belongs to another account. Each email can be used by one account only, so choose another address.
strings.rc_newPw2: Type the new app password again
strings.rc_noAcc: The account was not found on this device.
strings.rc_noMailPw: Only the email address. The app will never ask for your email account password, so do not type it here.
strings.rc_none: This account has no recovery email, so the password cannot be recovered.
strings.rc_ok: Email verified: {m}. Forgot your password? Tap "Forgot password" on the sign-in screen.
strings.rc_okNow: Email verified! You can now recover your password with it.
strings.rc_oneAcc: Each email can belong to one account only. Variants of the same inbox, such as capitals, Gmail dots or a +tag, count as the same email.
strings.rc_otherUser: The link belongs to {n}. Sign out first to use it.
strings.rc_rHint: Type the username and the recovery key from the email, and choose a new password. All data is kept.
strings.rc_removed: Email removed. Without it, a forgotten password cannot be recovered.
strings.rc_resendHint: A new email creates a new key, and the previous key stops working.
strings.rc_sent: Sent? Now open the email that arrived and type the key here.
strings.rc_stale: The key is right, but the saved data could not be opened. Send a new recovery email from a device where you are signed in.
strings.rc_step1: Tap "Open the email" and send it to yourself. You can also copy it and send it manually.
strings.rc_step2: When the email arrives, open it and type the recovery key from it here, or tap the link in the email.
strings.rc_where: Look in {m} for an email titled "Financial calculator · recovery key".

strings.src_envClaude: You are in the app inside Claude: there is no live connection here, so the last saved state is shown ({t}). On the website everything is live.
strings.src_envSite: You are on the website: data is pulled live from the sources.
strings.src_intro: Every number in the app, where it comes from, when it changed and why it may lag. People only see results; this screen is yours alone.
strings.src_pFail: Could not save the source. Try again.
strings.src_pickAll: The source you pick for each group applies to everyone using the app.

strings.src_pipe: How it works: on the website data is pulled live from the sources. A GitHub job also pulls the official data twice an hour and keeps a copy.
strings.src_w_binance: Refreshed every few seconds from Binance while the live connection is on.
strings.src_w_boi: The official rate is published once a business day (around 15:30), so during the day it differs from the market.
strings.src_w_boiInt: Changes only at a rate decision. Last: {d}. Next: {n}.
strings.src_w_boiRep: For official use (contracts, reports). Published once a business day.
strings.src_w_cbs: A monthly index published on the 15th of the next month at 18:30. The next one is due {n} and reaches the app by itself within half an hour.
strings.src_w_claude: Inside Claude there is no live connection, so this is the last copy saved for the app.
strings.src_w_closed: Trading is probably closed now, so the last closing price is shown.
strings.src_w_cnbc: Real-time trading rate, refreshed every 15 seconds while the screen is open.
strings.src_w_coinbase: Market rate from Coinbase, refreshed every second.
strings.src_w_crypto: Refreshed every second from Coinbase while the live connection is on.
strings.src_w_house: The home prices index naturally lags about two months, and the last three months are provisional. Next release due {n}.
strings.src_w_pickSnap: "Saved copy only" is picked: prices refresh twice an hour, not in real time.
strings.src_w_prov: The free data provider delays this by about 15 minutes (Tel Aviv exchange, gold and oil futures). Real-time data needs a paid exchange licence.
strings.src_w_rt: Real time, refreshed every 15 seconds while the screen is open.
strings.src_w_snap: No live connection right now, so the last saved rate is shown. The saved copy renews twice an hour on the website.
strings.src_w_snapMk: The live connection has not answered yet, so the saved copy is shown.
